prompt:
UI design mockup of the project screen of an AI software factory console, in its existing "Mission control" design: a near-black blue room (dark) or a warm cream day version (light), thin-bordered instrument panels with small corner marks, cyan as the system colour, amber as the one signal that needs a person, monospace figures, everything exact and calm. Desktop browser viewport, 16:9, flat, no browser chrome, no device frame, the screen fills the whole image.

The shell is fixed and must look like this: a quiet top bar ("Factory console", the project "ai-software-factory-code", links "Board", "New task", "Projects", "Resources", "Costs", "Policy", "Alerts", a theme toggle, "sebastian", "Log out"); under it the pulse band, one panel with the sentence "Two cards need your decision; #612's merge carries a migration." with an amber warning sign and a 3 px amber left rule, and under the sentence the instrument strip "● waiting on you | 3 working | 2 need you | €61.40 / €120.00 ▬▬▬▭▭ 51 % | GitHub: 1 open pull request"; then the main area: the chat on the left taking 40 percent of the width as the main region, and the board on the right taking 60 percent with its header row "Board", a small mono text box "Find: a word, #612, plan:558", "Wide view" and "?", and four columns: "Needs you 2" lit amber (a merge approval "Merge PR #612" with chips "high risk" "migration" and buttons "Approve", "Deny", "Split"; a question "#603 Which store for the session table?" with buttons "Postgres", "SQLite", "Ask the author"), "Queued 4", "In progress 5", "Done 8", each column head with a small ▾ at its right, the cards compact with a mono state row. No ticker at the foot.

What is new, and what this image is about: the chat holds many conversations, called threads. The content, spelled exactly. The open thread is titled "Session store: Postgres" and shows: you: "Why is #603 waiting?"; agent: "#603 asked which store the session table should use. The plan named Postgres; the brief allows SQLite for a single replica. I can answer Postgres for you."; a collapsed tool block "read card #603 · 0.4 s"; a proposal "I will: answer #603 with Postgres" with buttons "Do it" and "Skip". The threads, by last turn: "Inbox" (the factory's own thread, marked with an unread badge "2" and the newest line "Merge PR #612 waits for you: high risk, one migration"), "Plan: the members page" (a turn in flight, a small working mark, "14:26"), "Session store: Postgres" (open, "14:21"), "Costs read: the date window" ("yesterday"); and one archived thread "Export in pull request mode" shown last and dimmer. A "New" action for a new thread. The autonomy level of the project reads "assisted" and offers "manual", "assisted", "autonomous", "full auto". The composer at the chat's bottom: a prompt mark "›", the box "Ask or tell the project… (Enter sends, Shift+Enter breaks the line)", "Send", and a hint of the commands "/compact" and "/new". The browser tab's title would read "(2) Factory console".

Direction "Messenger": A messenger's conversation list inside the chat panel's left third, each thread a two-line row: a round mark (the factory's mark for "Inbox", the initial of the thread's first word otherwise), the title bold when unread, the newest line in the faint colour ("Merge PR #612 waits for you: high risk, one migration" under Inbox), the time at the right, an amber count badge "2" on Inbox, a cyan breathing dot on "Plan: the members page"; "Archived (1)" as a folded row at the bottom; "New" as a round "+" button at the list's top right. The level selector in the chat's head as a pill "assisted" that opens the four levels. The open thread's log on the right two thirds of the chat panel with the composer at its foot. Light theme: the cream day version of the same design, dark navy text on warm off-white panels, the same cyan and amber.

Legible UI text with exact spelling, nothing invented, no lorem ipsum. The pulse stays the loudest thing on the screen after the amber Needs you column; the chat stays the main region; the thread list and the level selector are quiet instruments, the unread badge and the working mark are the only loud marks on them. Made by a top product design studio. Not a template, not a generic admin dashboard.
